meaning: things to do, (as a suffix) to do..., made for...
sentence: 私に何か用ですか。
sentence_meaning: Do you need me for something?
mnemonic: Somebody has been stood in your doorway for a while now saying nothing at all, so in the end you have to be the one to ask. Yo. What is it you actually want? よう.
notes: 何か用ですか is do you need something. As a suffix it is made for: 子供用 for children. Same 用 as 用意 ようい.

sentence: 背中がかゆいです。
mnemonic: Two figures back to back, and 中 the dead centre of them. The one patch you cannot reach has itched since Tuesday. Senna? A car key? Anything: せなか.
notes: 背 on its own also does height: 背が高い is tall.

sentence: 私が髪を切ったのに、夫は気付きませんでした。
sentence_meaning: I cut my hair, but my husband didn't even notice.
mnemonic: 気 steam off a person and 付 a hand pressing something on until it sticks. Four inches came off her hair and by nine he has only asked where his keys are: きづく.
notes: に marks what you notice: 間違いに気付く. Same 付 as 付ける つける.

meaning: all of a sudden, without warning
sentence: 後ろからいきなり肩を叩かれた。
sentence_meaning: Someone suddenly tapped on my shoulder from behind.
mnemonic: A hand lands flat on your shoulder from behind and nobody made a sound getting there. Eek, and in a hurry, really: いきなり.
notes: The abrupt spoken one. 突然 とつぜん is the written version and 急に きゅうに is a state changing fast.

meaning: to carry across, to hand over
sentence: 彼に手紙を渡しました。
mnemonic: 氵 water, because this began as getting a thing over a river. She has been talking for an hour, so you put the glass into her hand: water, Sue. わたす.
notes: に marks who gets it: 彼に渡す. 渡る わたる is you crossing over yourself.

meaning: to be happy, to be delighted
sentence: 彼女はとても喜びました。
mnemonic: The drum and the mouth beneath it are making the same racket, and both meant to. She got the news at four and by six your local pub knows: よろこぶ.
notes: Used about other people being pleased. 嬉しい うれしい is how you say it about yourself.

sentence: 妹は可愛い服が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: My younger sister loves cute clothes.
mnemonic: 可 the yes you are permitted to give, and 愛 a heart carried about in the middle of it. The puppy has one ear inside out and is giving you the full cow eye: かわいい.
notes: Written in kana as often as not. かわいそう looks related but means poor thing, not cute.

sentence: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
mnemonic: 女 at 台 the platform again, except this time nobody pushed. The new job started at nine whether your coat was off or not. Ha, Jim, are you ready? はじまる.
notes: 始める はじめる is you starting it. 始まる is it starting, ready or not.

sentence: すてきな色のセーターですね。
sentence_meaning: That sweater is a wonderful color.
mnemonic: Nobody agrees what the two figures in this one are doing, so take the meaning and go. That jumper is a shade with no name and it has started a row: いろ.
notes: 色々 いろいろ is various, colours upon colours. 色 also reads しょく in compounds.

meaning: to recognize, to approve, to accept
sentence: 父が彼女との結婚を認めてくれました。
sentence_meaning: My father accepted my marriage to her.
mnemonic: 言 speech with 忍 endure under it, words held in until they have to come out. Her father set his glass down and said yes to the marriage: meet Tom, our lad. みとめる.
notes: Does recognising a fact, admitting it, and giving permission, all with one word. 間違いを認める is to admit a mistake.

sentence: 午後急に空が暗くなりました。
sentence_meaning: The sky suddenly got dark in the afternoon.
mnemonic: A hand snatching down at a heart, which is what the chest does. Four in the afternoon and the sky shuts like a lid while you cross the yard: きゅう.
notes: Same reading as 九 きゅう, nine. 急に きゅうに is the adverb and 急ぐ いそぐ is to hurry.

meaning: the other side, the other party, opponent
sentence: 友達は向こうにいます。
mnemonic: 向 the window that faces one way out, and this is whatever is at the other end of the look. Your friend is across the field, past the one moo cow: むこう.
notes: Also the other party in a deal or a fight. 向かう むかう heads that way, 向ける むける aims something, 向こう is the far end.

sentence: 子供は親の愛を求めます。
mnemonic: 求 a fur coat with the tails still on it and everybody in the village wanting it. She is not after the toy. What she is after costs nothing and is more to me: もとめる.
notes: More formal than ほしい. It does seeking, requesting and demanding: 助けを求める is to call for help.

sentence: 肩が痛いです。
mnemonic: 戸 a door hung on 月 the flesh, which is what this is: a hinge that takes the weight. You carried the bag on it all day and now it will not lift: かた.
notes: Same reading as 方 かた, the polite word for a person, and later 型 かた, a type or mould. 肩が凝る is stiff shoulders.

sentence: 彼には仲間がたくさんいる。
sentence_meaning: He has a lot of comrades.
mnemonic: 亻 a person right in 中 the middle of the group, with 間 the gap between them closed up. Nobody signed anything, they just kept turning up. Na, come on: なかま.
notes: Warmer than 友達 ともだち, and it works for a crew or a band. 仲がいい なかがいい is to get on well.

sentence: ようやくゴールが見えてきました。
sentence_meaning: At last, we could see the goal.
mnemonic: Six hours up the pass and the tent is finally in sight, with the yak that beat you there already sat down. Yo, yak, you: ようやく.
notes: The relief kind of at last. やっと is its close twin and does the same job in speech.

sentence: 嬉しくて思わず涙が出ました。
sentence_meaning: I was so happy I started crying without realizing it.
mnemonic: 田 a field on 心 a heart, and this time the heart got there first. The news landed and you were crying before any of it reached your head: oh, Moe was too. おもわず.
notes: A thing happening before you decided to do it. 思う おもう with the thinking taken out of it.

sentence: お金がほとんどありません。
mnemonic: The tin is out, the oven is hot, and there is not enough flour left in the bag to call it anything. Hot oven, no dough: ほとんど.
notes: With a negative it is hardly any, with a positive almost all. ほとんどない and ほとんど全部 both work.

sentence: 彼は突然走り出したのよ。
mnemonic: 穴 a hole with 犬 a dog bursting straight out of it, and 然 that being how things are. He was walking beside you, then he was forty yards up the road: とつぜん.
notes: The written and formal one. いきなり is the abrupt spoken version, 急に きゅうに is a state changing fast. Shares its 然 with 全然 and 当然.

sentence: 自分自身を疑ってはいけません。
mnemonic: 自 the nose you point at to mean me, with 身 a whole body drawn out in profile. Not your name and not your job. The one actually stood there: じしん.
notes: 自分自身 じぶんじしん doubles it for emphasis. Later comes 自信 じしん, self-confidence, which sounds identical and is written with 信.

sentence: 彼は再びここに戻ってきた。
sentence_meaning: He came back here once again.
mnemonic: You put the cat out at eleven, and at midnight there is a foot, a tabby, and the whole business to go through again: ふたたび.
notes: Written and a shade formal. また is the everyday again. 再 reads さい in compounds: 再会 さいかい.

sentence: 静かな所が好きです。
mnemonic: 青 fresh and still down the left side. Out at the end of the lane the loudest thing all afternoon is a car three fields off: she is a car, then nothing. しずか.
notes: 静かに しずかに is quietly. 静か takes な in front of a noun.

sentence: 鳥が飛んでいます。
mnemonic: It came off the fence post with no run-up at all and was over the hedge before you had the camera up. To boot, it took the sandwich: とぶ.
notes: Also jumping: 飛び込む とびこむ is to leap in. 跳ぶ is the spelling for jumping specifically.

sentence: 彼は歯が白い。
mnemonic: 白 the sun just clearing the horizon, the whitest thing going. He smiles and the pub goes quiet, and she, Roy, the lot of them, just stare: しろい.
notes: Also blank: 白紙 はくし is a blank sheet. 白 reads はく as well as しろ.

sentence: 昨日、父から手紙が届いた。
sentence_meaning: I received a letter from my father yesterday.
mnemonic: 尸 a shelter with 由 a channel running into it. The parcel arrives while you are out and sits on the step waiting for your toe to dock into: とどく.
notes: The thing arriving, not you sending it. 届ける とどける is you delivering it. 手が届く is to be able to reach something.
